utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case Number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, and good morning to you. Mr. Oric, good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you follow the proceedings in a language you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can, Your Honour. I can follow in the language I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down. Appearances, Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Jan Wubben, lead counsel for the Prosecution team, together with Ms. Patricia Sellers, co-counsel, and our case manager Ms. Donnica Henry-Frijlink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning. And appearances for Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. I am Vasvija Vidovic, assisted with Mr. John Jones, Defence counsel for Mr. Naser Oric, together here with us our legal assistant, Ms. Jasmina Cosic and our case manager, Mr. Geoff Roberts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, and good morning to you and your team. Any preliminaries before we bring in the witness. Yes, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. We have two small issues to raise preliminarily. And that would be to inform the Trial Chamber and learned counsel that we will be filing a motion for videolinks today. We would ask the Trial Chamber, if possible, whether they wanted to look at this motion prior to the break or not, but we wanted to file it in enough time that it could be reviewed. We understand that counsel certainly has a certain amount of time in which they're able to file their response, but just to announce that to the Trial Chamber. Also to state to the Trial Chamber. I believe that you're aware of correspondence that we're trying to resolve some of our 92(C) issues that pertain to witnesses whose statements who we would like to present to the Trial Chamber with the necessary omissions provided by Rule 92 bis (C). There is one issue concerning the appointment of a doctor, an order to look at one of our proposed candidates. I believe you're aware of that correspondence. It appears to me we need to finalise a decision on that. And I think Your Honour is also aware that we still have the issue of whether the person who is confirmed to be deceased is considered to be legally deceased by the Defence. We would just ask Your Honours in light of us trying to not only formulate our witness list but to be able to offer a schedule of witnesses that would be appropriate for the presentation of the Prosecution case and to facilitate the Victim Witness Unit and having them come up that we could appreciate if we could have some resolutions on some of the issues that are before you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And in addition for today, an issue I discussed with Madam Vidovic this morning, upon your request. The time to be allotted to Prosecution for examination and the Defence for their cross, we agreed upon two hours, including this opening for the Prosecution, and one hour and 55 minutes - I know it is some arithmetic - including the break, but one hour and 55 minutes for the Defence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So. I see that you are heeding our advice, and that's good to know. Let's not waste or lose -- not waste - sorry - lose more time. Let's get the witness in and get moving.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Eric, and welcome to this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: My name is Judge Carmel Agius. I come from Malta, and I am presiding over this trial against Naser Oric together with Judge Hans Henrik Brydensholt on my right and Judge Albin Eser on my left. Judge Brydensholt comes from Denmark and Judge Eser comes from Germany. Again once more, we welcome you. You are about to start giving evidence very soon, and before you do so our Rules require that you enter a solemn declaration equivalent to an oath, in the sense that in the course of your testimony you will be speaking the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text of this solemn declaration is contained on a piece of paper that you are being given now. Please read it out loud and that will be your solemn undertaking with us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you. Please take a chair. And I'll explain to you what's going to happen. You are -- hopefully we will do our utmost to finish with your testimony today so that you can go back to your home and to your work. You were first --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Turn it up please. I can't hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are first going to be asked a series of questions by Madam Sellers, who I presume you have already met and she then will be followed by Madam Vidovic, who is lead counsel for accused Naser Oric. May I just remind you you are a professional man and for me it becomes easier to explain this. You have a responsibility under your oath to speak the truth and the whole truth, not only when you are being asked questions by the Prosecutor, who has summoned you here as a witness, but also when you are being asked questions by the Defence counsel. Your responsibility does not change. In other words, you don't have a right to discriminate in favour or against one of the parties. Yes, Ms. Sellers, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And on the basics you can go direct, who he is, when what he does, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I was just about to ask permission could I lead him in the interest of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are granting you permission straight away.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Examined by Ms. Sellers:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Eric.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [In English] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please confirm that, Mr. Eric, you were born in Serbia I believe in 1964, you were raised in the village of Kravica in the municipality of Bratunac. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you ethnically a Bosnian Serb.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [In English] Serbian. Serb, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You studied medical technology in Tuzla and then worked as a medical technician in the Bratunac health centre between 1987 and 1992.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Completed the higher medical school in Tuzla, section for laboratory technicians, and I worked from 1987 to 1992 until the outbreak of the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then did you decide to return to Kravica 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the village of Kravica, it's situated in a valley, isn't it, Mr. Eric?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does the main road that passes by Kravica lead to the north toward Zvornik or to the north-east towards Tuzla and does it lead in the south-east direction to the town of Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also, I'd like to ask you, are the Bosnian Serb hamlets of Jezestica, Siljkovici, Batkovici, Obradici, and Djermani located in the hills above and surrounding Kravica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it mainly a Bosnian Serb town?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you also confirm for Your Honours that in 1992 Kravica was a village of about 600 inhabitants?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Around about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... from Bratunac with your immediate family?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your grandparents in 1992 live in Kravica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like you to explain to the Trial Chamber what type of work did you do upon your work to Kravica.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: I started working in the infirmary as a medical technician. In fact, before that time the doctor and the nurse used to come there once or twice a week. After the outbreak of the war that stopped and then when I returned to Kravica I continued in that job that I used to do before.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note that counsel should wear headphones and watch out for the interpretation so we don't overlap.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Certainly. I would like to note that there is a problem with my interpretation. It is going up and down. So could I just be given one second please -- oh, now it's in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, could you please describe precisely what did the clinic in Kravica look like.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: It is a smaller building. It had one room as a pharmacy, one examination for the doctor, and a larger room that was a kind of surgery, where smaller minor surgeries were performed, shots were given, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you work in the clinic with other doctors?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who worked with you in the clinic, Mr. Eric?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: I was alone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a Mr. Tomic who worked there?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Marko Tomic was a driver.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he drive for the clinic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: He did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, were you aware that there was a general mobilisation when you left Bratunac and returned to Kravica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a result of that mobilisation, did you receive any weapons such as a gun or a rifle?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a result of that mobilisation, did you receive a uniform?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as a result of that mobilisation, did you report to a commanding officer for duty?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you returned to Kravica to work in the medical clinic, you did not return to Kravica necessarily as a member of an armed forces that worked at the medical. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Correct. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, were there tensions between Muslims and Serbs in the municipality of Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of villages or hamlets where Muslims were expelled from in April, May, or June 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of villages or hamlets where Serbs were expelled from during that same period?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, is it because of the tensions in the surrounding area of Kravica that your wife and children decided to leave Kravica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And likewise, as a result of the tension did villagers in Kravica organise a village guard?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, would you please tell the Trial Chamber whether the members of the village guard were regular members of the armed forces or not.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, does that mean that they were not members of the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge -- I'm sorry. My interpretation is down again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, we are not having the -- we are not encountering the problem. At least let me speak for myself. I am not encountering a problem. Judge Eser, are you having problems with the interpretation?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Okay, I'm fine again. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please draw my attention as soon as there is a repetition because there could be some technical hitch or something.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Certainly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. If necessary, then you can -- so that we don't lose time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Switch microphones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, I would like to ask you: Did the village guard in Kravica and in the surrounding hamlets set up a line of defence?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would ask the usher to please show Mr. Eric Prosecution Exhibit, this is the one for Mr. Eric, it's a map. Your Honours, I'm going to ask that this map be tendered but I would ask Mr. Eric to make a couple markings on the map prior to that and then I will ask for the number so it can be put in evidence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Eric, I believe you will have to look at the map on the ELMO, that's to your left next to the usher. Could I please ask you to look that way.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [In English] Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you place an "X" on the village of Kravica.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please put that "X" in a circle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please draw a circle around the "X."

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And to the right of that circle, could you please put your initials. Or just below it. Just below it where there is that open space.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. You have testified that there was a line of village guards. And did the line include the village or the hamlet of Siljkovici.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you mark on the map where Siljkovici is.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, would you want him to put an S for each name of a town that is different? We might run into a little bit of alphabetical difficulties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you turn that "X" into a star, please. So that we don't have two Xs. Yeah, okay. No, no, no. The other one leave it as it is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So for the record we now have a star denoting the location of Siljkovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, did the line of defence also include the hamlet of Mijina Bara which is above Jezestica.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now would you please mark that with a "J."

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But you need to put a "Y" or a "J".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you mark a "J" there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did the defence line also include the hamlet of Djermani?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [In English] Djermani, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please put a "G" where Djermani is.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And your initials, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also, did the defence line include the hamlet of Magasici.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [In English] Magasici, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please mark an "M" there with your initials.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the defence line also include the hamlet of Mandici?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also please mark that with "MA" and your initials, please.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the defence line also include the hamlet of Popovici?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please mark that with a "P" and your initials.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did the defence line include Banjevici?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please mark that with a "BV" and your initials.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the defence line also include Brana Bacici?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: English Brana Bacici, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you mark that.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you put "BB."

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the defence line also include Donja Bacici?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please mark "DB" and your initials.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why did you put it there and not at 5.00 o'clock?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's approximately. I don't know how to find my way around the map precisely but this is approximately it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, do you see that mark on the map a little bit to the lower right-hand side from where you were? Do you see that? Could you answer yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I would now ask you, was the hamlet of Jezero included in the line of defence?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please mark that on the map --

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Here it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you mark "JV" and then initial, please.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Eric, this line of defence, was this a line that was constructed and ordered to attack, or was this a line that was constructed and ordered to defend the villages and hamlets that we've just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I did not receive interpretation of his reply.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could I ask the witness the question again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, would you please inform the Trial Chamber whether this line of defence that you have just drawn and the villages included, was that a line of defence in order to mount attacks or in order to defend the villages and hamlets that we just spoke about?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: To defend them, to defend them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Eric, would you tell me about how many village guards manned these defence lines.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: About four, 500, perhaps more. Maybe 350. I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would they be on the defence line 24 hours a day at all times or do they work in shifts?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: In shifts. If there were 27 people in Siljkovici, for example, 10 or 15 were on the line and half of them were resting. They would change places.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you yourself ever go up to the line of defence to stand guard?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No. Maybe I did go once, put I didn't -- I didn't really go. I wasn't part of the guard duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would ask you to look at the map again and to answer the following question: Were there any gaps or weak spots in the line of defence that you have drawn for us? Would you please look at the map and tell us were there any weak spots and where were they.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were some near Hranca, in this part, and there were some at Kostan above Siljkovici. These are Bare around here somewhere. It wasn't linked. And also this part here -- of course this part here was facing towards the Drina river.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could I please ask Mr. Eric to mark on the map --

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [In English] Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's okay. Where Hranca and Kostan and then the third area you just testified about. Could you please mark that with the first letter --

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Hranca. And which mark should I use?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "H" is fine, with your initials.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you mentioned Kostani?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Kostani, yes, it's around here. It's somewhere on the map but I don't know where it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you mentioned a third area.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: There was no need to close it there, because the way out was towards the Drina, Ocavici [phoen], Banjevici, towards Sopotnik. There were no Muslim villages behind that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would seek now to tender the map into evidence. I believe that we do need a number for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Just one matter, Your Honour. We would appreciate clarification of what these lines are on the map because we were a bit puzzled by them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And we saw them on another map that we had available last week actually --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I might be able to enlighten you literally. I understand those are utility lines, that they are lines dealing with electrical installations. And I would like to certainly assure learned counsel and Your Honours they will not be part of our testimony. We are in no way indicating that they represent something that is at this point relevant to our presentation of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you satisfied with that, Mr. Jones?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This will be exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: P396, thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Eric, is it correct that you continued to work at the clinic in Kravica from the month of May and throughout the month of July?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Trial Chamber what types of patients did you receive at the clinic and what types of medical treatment did you have to perform.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: In the beginning these were civilians and soldiers. And then later when the fighting started and when the conflict became more intense, there were more and more wounded. These were wounded people who were injured in the places where fighting was going on, in the different places where fighting was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of the fighting that took place in Glogova in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you treat anyone from that fighting at your clinic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was one wounded person. Yes, I applied bandages and he was released.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you yourself take part in the fighting in Glogova in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In July of 1992, did you receive a call at the clinic for medical assistance to go near Glogova?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you go there with your colleague, Mr. Tomic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I went there because I was told that we had one wounded person and one dead person -- one seriously wounded person. Tomic and I went together with Slavko Nikolic, Milan Nikolic and two other men to take care of these people, and they brought them in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were the wounded person and the dead person, were these people who had participated in some kind of military action?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No, no. They did not. I think some explosive device, a bomb, was thrown into their trench on the line that they were defending.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did you and Mr. Tomic then take the person to the Bratunac medical centre, the same centre where you had worked previously?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes. All of us, all the people that I mentioned took that person, the wounded person, to Bratunac and handed him over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after you handed the person over at the Bratunac medical centre, did you, your driver, and the other people you've mentioned return toward the direction of Glogova?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes. We were returning back to Kravica, passing through Glogova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you ambushed on the way back?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes. We were ambushed at the entrance to Glogova. I can show you that on the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. We'll do that in second. I'd like you to explain first to Your Honours how the ambush took place.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: We were going back in the car, Marko Tomic was driving and the rest of us were sitting in the car. We were returning to Magasici in order to take over this dead person so that we could make all the burial arrangements. But at the entrance of Glogova on the left side as you come from Bratunac, they opened fire on us. Marko Tomic was wounded, I wounded, Slavko Nikolic was wounded, Milan Nikolic was wounded, the person who was sitting in front of me was killed, and the person who was sitting next to Marko Tomic was not injured. We continued on our way towards Kravica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would now ask the usher to please show Mr. Eric Prosecution Exhibit, I believe it's been marked 394 from our previous use. I would like to tell the Trial Chamber that I'm going to ask Mr. Eric to mark on this map also and then we'll have to ask for another number before we tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Incidentally, Ms. Sellers, while we do the administrative part, together with the statement that supposedly the witness released -- made to the Prosecution, to the Office of the Prosecutor, there is also another statement dated supposedly 5th of February, 1994, with a sequitur dated February 1994, a supplementary statement, supposedly released to the government Ministry of the Interior, Sarajevo security, but this is not the same person?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I would like to inform you that is not the same person. In an abundance of caution, since it has the same name, we provided it. But if one would look at the birth dates, and if one would actually look at some of the contents, it is not the same person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The parents' names are different, date of birth is different, and the events also are different. So I just wanted to bring this up. And, Mr. Jones, I mean, we are definitely not even looking at those other statements because we take it they are not the same ones, they are not from the same person.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, that's what we concluded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I was under the impression that someone had marked -- put markings on P394. We already have --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I understand that possibly one of the previous Prosecution witnesses might have marked on this map. We're more than willing now to offer the map that Mr. Eric will use as a new exhibit because he also will mark on it and to just give it a different identification and tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I am under the impression, like Ms. Sellers, that someone -- one of the witnesses did put some marks on that, but I may be wrong. Let's proceed. I mean, it seems that the map that the registrar has doesn't contain any markings on it. So we can either use that, or if you prefer to tender the big map that Madam Usher is holding in her hands --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would prefer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We can proceed with that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would prefer the bigger map, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And that would be 398.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be 397.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 397. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Eric, you see the map that is in front of you now. Could you please for purposes of simplicity, please mark Kravica again on that map with a "K."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Does he need to mark it? Just point at it. Don't write anything there. Just point at Kravica, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And for the record the Chamber notices that the witness has pointed at Kravica on the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Right. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would ask now, Mr. Eric -- please don't mark anything on the map now, Mr. Eric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please don't put anything on the map until or unless we tell you or ask you. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I already did put a mark on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like you to show the Trial Chamber what is the road that you and Mr. Tomic took in the van to arrive at Kravica to where you picked up the wounded person.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: From Bratunac through Repovac, Hranca, Glogova, and then this is a place called Avdagina Njiva, up the hill. Magasici is to the left. We did not reach Magasici because we were wounded on that road, here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... excuse me, first I want you to show the road between Kravica and Bratunac that you took. Starting with Kravica, please. Yes, you can mark on the map.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Kravica. Yes, it's here. I am marking it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, where did you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, the witness has marked in black over what appeared to be a road leading -- on the map leading from Kravica to Glogova and from Glogova to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please indicate where you picked up the wounded person on that road on your way to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Somewhere around here, near Magasici. Somewhere about here, as far as I can find my way on the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please mark an "M" at that spot with your initials, please.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Eric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, coming back from Bratunac on your way back to Kravica, would you please indicate on the map where the ambush took place.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: We were returning from Bratunac. We passed through Repovac, Hranca. At the entrance to Glogova there is a bridge there. I don't know if I will indicate it precisely on the map, but it was somewhere around here, the place where we were wounded. That's where the ambush was. On the left side, as you're going from Bratunac to Kravica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. For the record, the witness indicates the spot where the ambush, according to his version, took place by means of a black square which crosses the road that leads from Bratunac to Glogova and against which he put his initials "CE." Could you put your initials, please, against that black square. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [In English] Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the place you have mentioned, Hranca, is that one of the weak spots on the defensive lines that you testified about earlier today, Mr. Eric?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes. Ambushes were set up in that place before and also after I was wounded. This was a place -- there's a creek there and we would -- never managed quite to -- because of this creek, this is where they passed through and entered Glogova. There was shooting on the 2nd of July and also there was another ambush in August after I was wounded in the same place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please mark where Hranca is on this map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please. With your initials.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you stated that they would often attack or have ambushes, who are you referring to when you state "they"?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Muslims. I think these were soldiers, Muslims, members of these Muslim units. I don't know what they were called at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you and Mr. Tomic and the other men in the van return to Kravica after the ambush?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. Were you then taken to Bratunac and later removed to a hospital?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. We were not able to because there was an ambush in that part. There was no way to go back. We -- can I explain to you where we had to go in order to reach a place where we would be given medical treatment? It's almost 40 kilometres away -- I'm not sure if it's 40 kilometres but...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... show Your Honours on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He could just indicate to us where he went and that's it and then we will --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, that's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you indicate to Your Honours where you went after our injuries.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Opravdici, Popovici, Ocenovici, Banjevici, Sopotnik. And then along the Drina, all this way to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's your testimony that you had to take this road along the Drina to get back to Bratunac. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would ask now that the usher remove the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Eric, were you hospitalised in Serbia because of the wounds that you received in the ambush?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would ask the usher now to hand Mr. Eric exhibit -- I believe there are copies that have been provided. I would apologise that we don't have a translation of the exhibit, but I believe that it will be fairly self-explanatory. It can be seen on Sanction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is my release form when I was released from the hospital -- discharge certificate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you give the Prosecution a copy of this hospital form last week?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is this an exact copy of that form?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is something that can be checked in Loznica. They probably have that in their records.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you stated that you were in Loznica. Now, Loznica is located in which country?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: In Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So was it common practice that the hospitals in Serbia would receive and treat the wounded from Bosnia during this time period?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Well, since we only had the Zvornik hospital where wounded could be treated as in-patients, as the conflict was becoming more and more intense, this hospital could not deal with all of the wounded. So they had to be sent to Loznica, Belgrade. Those people from Skelani had to go to -- all the way to Uzeci [phoen] and Valjevo, because in Skelani they didn't even have an in-patient ward.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at the form, would you confirm to Your Honours the dates of your stay in the hospital in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: From the 28th of July, 1992, until the 10th of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the date of -- that the ambush took place, Mr. Eric?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: On the 28th of July, 1992, the same day that I was admitted to hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would ask to have this marked, given a number, and I would ask to tender this into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this would be 398, no? This is 398, please, P398.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, did you give an interview to the Office of the Prosecution in April of 2001?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that interview, did you tell the investigators about the ambush that took place near Hranca?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Gamini was the gentleman who came. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are the facts that you've testified about today before Your Honours the facts that you remember concerning the ambush that took place on the 28th of July, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Eric, when you left the hospital in Serbia, did you learn that the hamlet of Jezestica had been attacked?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes. I heard that from people who were exposed to this attack. They told me about it. They said that the village was attacked on that day, that the neighbours, Muslims, attacked them, and that about -- I don't know the exact number of how many people were killed that day. But Hanjel Komlajenovic [phoen] had had his head cut off that day. This is what they told me. This is a person who was a year younger than I am, and he went to school with my brother. He was born in 1965. This is all I that found out about this attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you learn which forces attacked the hamlet of Jezestica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes. These neighbours, Muslim neighbours, from around there. They recognised some of them, the people who were attacked recognised that there were some people there from Jaglici, Cizmici and other villages around there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Eric, when you say the word "neighbours," does that mean these people were not part of a fighting force, that they were just neighbours from the next village?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: They were part of the forces, yes, but they were also neighbours. People recognised them. These villages bordered one another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you learn at any time about the troop strength, the numbers of the Muslim forces that were engaged in this attack?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear at any time of who was considered, if anyone, to be the commander of the Muslim forces that either ambushed you in Glogova or that attacked Jezestica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No. Except that there was talk and it was said on radio and TV that it was Naser Oric. But we didn't have any reliable information, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this was just information that was basically a type of common knowledge. Is that correct, Mr. Eric?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Eric, between July and December of 1992 did you continue to work at the clinic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. When I recovered from my wounds, I continued to work, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, during the course of your working months at the clinic in Kravica, did you know a Jovan Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What role, if any, did Jovan Nikolic have in the organisation of the village guards in Kravica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: I don't know. Once the combat operations started, a group of people came to our village or gathered in our village who were military officers or people who had a good reputation among the Serbian people in order to organise defence of the village and all of the things that go along with that. And he was one of -- he was a member of that group. He was one of those people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have meetings with Jovan Nikolic at the elementary school in Kravica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes. We met two or three times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So would you state that you attended these meetings on a regular basis or is two or three times a rather small set of meetings compared to the meetings that were held?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, two or three times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So does that mean it was on a regular basis?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, is Jovan Nikolic related to you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: He is a close relative. In fact, he is my uncle, my father's brother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Eric, in 1992, November precisely, was the Kravica Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade formed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If he is his father's brother, how is it that his family name is not Eric and it's Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have not inquired into those types of relations. I've asked --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can explain that. He's actually not my father's brother; he is a cousin. He is a cousin. They are not sons of the same mother. No, that's not what I meant to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, turning your attention to November of 1992, was the Kravica Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade formed at that time?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: That's not the way I would put it. That unit looked like a battalion at that time in November.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, as a result of the formation of the unit of the battalion, how did things change in terms of how the village guard functioned?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Perhaps a little better, but mainly the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive more uniforms, for example?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive more weapons or heavy machinery?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No. No, we had to do with what we had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, at the medical clinic, did you receive at least more medical supplies?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Oh, that we did. I went to that meeting of that so-called group, whatever you want to call it, I don't know what name to put on it, to inquire about medical equipment and vehicles that we needed. At that time a man from Holland donated a van with medication.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would ask the usher now to hand Mr. Eric another form that Your Honour has not been tendered into evidence. I would ask for a number so we could pre-identify it for the future. This form has been translated into English. Have you handed Mr. Eric the form?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, do you recognise this document that's in front of you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is a decision to recognise my wartime service, the time I spent with the army during the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you give the Prosecution a copy of the original document last week?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: I provided the original.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And is this an exact copy of that original that you gave the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is. It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Eric, on this form on the bottom of the first page it states that you spent a total of four years and 12 days participating in the Yugoslav armed forces of the Republika Srpska. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It also states that five months -- further down on the bottom of the page, that five months were outside the zone of combat and that 43 months were within the zone of combat. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the time that we have been speaking about this morning considered part of the time that was within the zone of combat?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes. But these five months, that was the 30th April, 1996. It was before the Dayton Accord. It's just that the combat operations had seized and there was an interim period before I started working in my company again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Mr. Eric, with this document is it correct that even though you were not issued uniforms or weapons or that you reported directly to a commander, during the period that we've spoken about this morning, that Republika Srpska, for purposes of disability, will recognise this as a period of service?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: This is a document which proves that I had been in the army, and I don't use it for other purposes than to calculate and benefit from a pension.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just for the record, it's not that important, but just for the record I noticed that in the original, Ms. Sellers, on the left top part where it says -- after the reference Bratunac, it's 20 February, and then it's 2001 on the printed form. But there is a number 2 typewritten which hints the possibility that this document goes back to 2002 and not to 2001. I don't know. I mean, it's ...

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I note where Your Honour is referring to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think it can be 20th February, 2001, because if you go further down the page on the original it refers to a date, which is the 16th of August, 2001, which purportedly is when the witness made his request. So I mean, just for the record, I think it's the case of altering the text of the translation to read 20th February, 2002, instead of 20th February, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: That is noted, Your Honour. We will alter that text and recirculate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just for the record. It's not going to change anything, but just to make sure everything is no order.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Otherwise is there -- are there any remarks on the part of the Defence on this document? If I don't take any remarks or a position from your side, I take that there is none and I admit the document. That's the procedure that I adopt, okay? That we adopt, rather. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would just ask that this now be given a number and this becomes Prosecution Exhibit...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, were you -- did you hold any rank, any formal rank, during the time period that we have discussed today between April and November of 1992 within any army formation?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. Mr. Eric, were you a member of the SDS political party in 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Well, it's possible that I feature somewhere on their lists, but I was never a front line member of the SDS. But I was a Serb in 1992, and that implied that I would be in the ranks of the SDS. I don't know if there were any exceptions, but not in our area. If you were a Muslim you were in SDA; if you were a Serb, you were in SDS. I was in the first post-war list of nominees for the Municipal Assembly of Bratunac, and I was a partisan of that party, a supporter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Mr. Eric, could I also ask you that during the same time period that we're speaking of today, 1992, were you a member of the Crisis Staff in Kravica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: If you look in terms of establishment, if you call it the Crisis Staff, then yes. Although I was there only in terms of establishment formally because units, starting with the platoon with every army, have within their organisation a person who is in charge of medical affairs. And since this was at the level of battalion or beyond in terms of establishment you had to have that position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Ms. Sellers. Was it municipal Crisis Staff or was it a SDS Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was talking about the military headquarters, military head staff -- military staff in Kravica. I was never in the municipal SDS as far as politicals are concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But I'm referring to the Crisis Staff. There was a Crisis Staff --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you can call it the Crisis Staff. We can call it that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe Your Honour wanted to know: Were you in the Crisis Staff in the village of Kravica or in the municipality of Bratunac? Did you belong to a Crisis Staff in Kravica or in the municipality of Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Only for the village of Kravica. In terms of establishment, I was part of that Crisis Staff, if you wish to call it that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it because that you had training as a medical laboratory technician and that you worked at the clinic that you were part of this member of the Crisis Staff in Kravica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: A moment ago I said that every military unit, and everybody who served in the army knows this, every unit from the lowest to the highest level has within its composition certain personnel in charge of medical affairs and medical service. And I was that medical man, if you want to accept the term that was common in our environment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We may not be fine-tuned. I'm not convinced as yet that he is strictly speaking referring to a Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it could be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think the notion of a Crisis Staff as we have heard it in this Tribunal from one case to another has been pretty uniform. The witness is -- in my opinion, may be confusing the notion of a Crisis Staff with something that to him is equivalent to a Crisis Staff but which to us is not exactly what is a Crisis Staff. Who else was on this Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had in mind the people who were dealing with organising the defence of the village. Those are the people I meant. Do you understand me now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Was the head of the police of Kravica on the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was no police in Kravica. There was no police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Was there a representative of the police in -- on the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no way. People from the village organised themselves to defend the village and made up a group that was in charge, that led the defence of the village. You can call them what you want.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who was in charge -- who was presiding over this Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was nobody at the head. Everybody together managed it. There was my 70-plus old grandfather who was part of that Crisis Staff because he had participated in the Second World War and had some knowledge and some skills. So we're not talking here about an organised unit with, you know, men or ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But the Crisis Staffs were something that were contemplated under your law, under your system, to become operative in moments of crisis, like when there is an earthquake, for example, or like when there is a war. Was this an organised Crisis Staff or was it just an informal Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was an informal Crisis Staff. I had never heard of it before as having been established and awaiting the beginning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who asked you to be part of this Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nobody asked me. They put me on that list and twice or thrice I went to attend the meeting, and they just asked me questions of my area of expertise, the provision of medical services.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who are they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, these people. For instance, my grandfather, that Jovan Nikolic. There was a turnover of people. Some got killed. There was Raso Milosevic, for instance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And where were meetings held?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the schoolhouse.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, for that clarification.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would now like to draw your attention, Mr. Eric, to the 24th of December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Again, I would ask Your Honours could I lead the witness during part of this background information so that we may be able to proceed as rapidly as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Jones or Ms. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, I think if it's approached with caution. We can't obviously give a blanket agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, was the village of Glogova attacked on the 24th of December, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any fighting in that village on December 24th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, in May of 1992, was the village of Glogova the scene of fighting, as you testified earlier?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, minor fighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that time were there Muslims who were expelled from the village of Glogova?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on December 24th, 1992, did fighting in the village of Glogova occur between Muslim forces and Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell the Trial Chamber: To your knowledge, which forces attacked the village of Glogova on the 24th of December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: It was attacked by Muslim forces and on the same day it was captured by these forces. They also cut off the Kravica-Bratunac road on the same day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Jovan Nikolic participate in the fighting in Glogova?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that you did not participate in the fighting in Glogova?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would ask the usher to hand Mr. Eric the map that we previously used, a coloured map, number 397.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, you've previously marked on this map --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, do we have that up on the screen -- on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, you previously marked on this map the length of the road between Kravica and Bratunac and you also showed the Trial Chamber where Glogova was on this map. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Eric, when the Muslim forces recaptured Glogova, did it affect the main road between Kravica and Bratunac that you previously marked?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please show Your Honours where the road was affected.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Well, roughly like this. Here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Eric, when I'm using the word "affected" does that mean that it was impossible for Bosnian Serb forces to use the road now to travel between Kravica and Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: It was not possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think for the record the witness has drawn a line across the road between Bratunac and Glogova roughly halfway -- halfway. Could I ask you, sir, to put your initials against that line please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Complies].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And he has affixed his initials "SE" to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, what road now, if any, had to be taken to establish a link between Kravica and Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No, no. We couldn't go to Bratunac using this road. We had to go round about. For instance, when I was wounded it went something like this: Kravica, Opravdici, then Ocenovici, Sopotnik, like this. This is the road you had to take to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you also put your initials where you just marked that road.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And Your Honours if the record could reflect that now the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. For the record, the witness indicates a route starting from Kravica going north to the direction of Borodnik -- Sopotnik and then following the river Drina right down to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Eric, as a result of the Muslim recapture of Glogova, were Kravica and the Bosnian Serb hamlets that you identified earlier in your testimony and marked on the first map, were they now surrounded by Bosnian Muslim hamlets?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would those Bosnian Muslim hamlets be hamlets such as Konjevic Polje, Sandici, Grabosko --

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Grabovska you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Grabovska. Pavici?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the territory of Paljevic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Right. Right. All this was kept by the Muslims, held by the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would now ask you, Mr. Eric, to turn to the map and would you please mark for Your Honours the towns that I have indicated or the areas. We'll go again. Konjevic Polje. "KP." Would you please mark "KP" on the map and your initials.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please mark Sandici on the map and your initials. With an "S," please.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: There is no Sandici on this map because they are somewhere around here. I'll mark it. "S" for Sandici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you also mark Grabosko, please.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Well, there is no Grabovska either, but there is Urkovici. I'll put a "G" for Grabovska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Is Urkovici near what you referred to before as Grabovska?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes. They are very close.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you now mark Pavici with a "P"?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Pavici is somewhere in this area probably. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please mark on the map Mecave?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Mecave. Mecave is also in the vicinity. I don't know how well I'll manage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you put your initials.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. For the record -- and that's because on the map there is more than one "M" encircled indicated by the same witness on the same map. Could I have the map --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is what I mean. Here's Mecave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The witness has indicated -- has put on "M" together with his initials in reply to the Prosecution's witness -- question. Just beneath Paljevici and to the left of Sopotnik. Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, could I also ask you to indicate on the map the territory that is referred to as Paljevic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, is it your testimony that the towns you have just marked Konjevic Polje, Sandici, Grabovska, Pavici, Mecari, and the territory of Paljevici are Muslim villages or hamlets that surrounded Kravica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, might I ask you --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And Your Honours I will be concluding this section.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And we will have a break.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That as a result of the attack on the 24th of December and the recapture of Glogova by the Muslim forces that Kravica was cut off from the normal route of communication to Bratunac and was also surrounded in the west by Bosnian Muslim villages. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would ask at this time to tender the map. I believe it already is into evidence but the usher may remove the map. Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's already tendered in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Fine. Your Honours, I will be moving to a new section of this. I think this would be an appropriate time if you wanted to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's try to stick to a 25-minute break and try to be as punctual as possible okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, before the break you confirmed that Kravica was cut off from the normal route to Bratunac and that also it was surrounded in the west by Bosnian Muslim villages as a result of the December 24th recapture of Glogova by the Muslim forces. My question to you now is then: After December 24th, did the Bosnian Serbs in Kravica anticipate that there might be a Muslim attack on the village? It appears that interpretation is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see that there is something wrong. [Microphone not activated] Could -- yes, something happened in the meantime, because even mine was switched off --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It seems there was something wrong because even mine was switched off.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can hear you now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But you did not hear the question, no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I will repeat the question. Ms. Sellers asked you the following: "Mr. Eric, before the break you confirmed that Kravica was cut off from the normal route to Bratunac and that also it was surrounded in the west by Bosnian Muslim villages as a result of the December 24th recapture of Glogova by the Muslim forces. My question to you now is then: After December 24th, did the Bosnian Serbs in Kravica anticipate that there might be a Muslim attack on the village?" That is the question that you need to answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We assumed so, but we were not sure because we were attacked by Muslim forces before on major Serbian holidays. So it was to be expected that it could happen that day, but nobody knew that for sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, what was the strength of the village guards in Kravica and the surrounding hamlets in that time period?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: In December, perhaps about 350 to 400. Well, as it happens in war, some people left, some people were wounded. So I think it was about 350 to 400. I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were reinforcements sent from Bratunac to Kravica, that area, to strengthen the number of village guards?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No. Except for about 40 people who came from Bratunac. There were some people from Bijeljina there and the military police, but nobody else came other than they.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Mr. Eric, is it your testimony that reinforcements from outside of the area totalled around 40 persons?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did there come a time period when Kravica and the surrounding Bosnian Muslim hamlets were attacked by the forces, the Muslim forces -- I'm sorry, the surrounding Bosnian Serb hamlets - if you could correct the transcript, please - were attacked by the Bosnian Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes. On the 7th early in the morning I was woken up by loud shooting, accompanied by loud detonations. We had an alarm siren which was activated. I went straight to the medical -- to the health centre because my house is about 300 metres away from that facility. I stayed there the whole day throughout the entire attack except for going to the school twice to see what happened with the help that was promised regarding the transport. Because from hour to hour the number of the wounded that I had was growing and I had no means to transport them. I was told that some vehicles would arrive, maybe a helicopter, but there was nothing. Then the second time when I went to the school I told this young man there who was attending the military academy, Lazar Ostojic. I said: Lazar, what am I going to do? My number of wounded is growing. He said: Slavisa, I don't know. Try to evacuate them as best you can. That's what I did. I went to the medical centre and I told them to lead those people out. There were leaving one by one. Four remained behind who were not able to walk. They couldn't be moved. I was standing in front of the building and those last few people who were passing by, I asked them to carry these people. The last person I actually helped to carry out, Zeljko Jankovic, we left. We were dodging bullets between the houses and we left towards Opravdici. This was maybe around 3.00 or 3.30 in the afternoon. I can't tell you the exact time when we actually left, when we were evacuated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Before we proceed I want a confirmation from you, particularly from the Defence because the Prosecution are always here, we are scheduled to be sitting tomorrow and Thursday in the afternoon. Would you agree to shift it to the morning instead of the afternoon or do you have commitments?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I think that would be fine with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So we will be sitting in the morning tomorrow and Thursday. Friday was in the morning in any case, and we will be sitting in Courtroom II.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. And Wednesday in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no. Today in Tuesday already.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: My apologies. Thursday in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Don't confuse me, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: My apologies. I'm with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is it okay with you, Ms. Sellers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that will be fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, just a confirmation to be sure. Tomorrow afternoon as well?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no. Tomorrow and Thursday, instead of sitting in the afternoon, we will sit in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So there's a switch. And this witness for today, Your Honour, is still projected to finalise today?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
