utterances.text: Thank you, confirmation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So Gerold, could you proceed. Yes, sorry for the interruption.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: That's okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, you testified that the attack began on the 7th. Was that the 7th of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that a special day?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was Christmas. That is the most important Orthodox holiday which is celebrated in the family. It's a family holiday, Christmas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, you also testified that you spoke to Mr. Lazar Ostojic. Who was this person?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was a young man whom I knew. He was there for Christmas. You could say that he was in command. He was a member of the military academy. He was attending the military academy. He's born from that area, so he was there in the school. He was sort of in command. He was there in the school and there were means of communication there. So I went and I asked him what I should do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Ostojic more or less replace Jovan Nikolic in terms of the role or function he performed in Kravica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Something like that, yes. Something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Eric, during the attack did you spend most of your time at the medical clinic attending to the wounded that came in because of the attack?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stated that you finally left the clinic with some of the people who were wounded and you went into the direction of Opravdici. Why did you go toward Opravdici?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Because that was the only way towards the Drina where we thought there were no Muslims, and this turned out to be right during the course of our withdrawal. These were all Serbian villages and we passed by there towards Sopotnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, I believe I asked you to mark Opravdici on one of the first maps we looked at this morning. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, does Opravdici, is it situated an elevation above Kravica, which you testified before is in a valley?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you observe from your position, Opravdici, what was happening in the town of -- the village of Kravica as you evacuated?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Not quite. We could see what was happening in Siljkovici, because that is at an elevation compared to Kravica, and we could see the village of Kravica burning, we could see the cattle thereabouts. There are also some trees in between, so you couldn't really have the best view of it but it was possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified that the village of Kravica was burning. To your knowledge, did the Bosnian Serb forces set the village of Kravica on fire as they were retreating?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Serbs, no, no. No. I was amongst the last to leave. So, no, it wasn't the Serbs. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge was the village of Kravica set on fire by Bosnian Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I wonder if my learned friend could simply ask to who to the witness's knowledge set the village on fire. It's a very leading way of putting it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I can rephrase the question. I certainly withdraw it and will rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think that would be most helpful, Ms. Sellers. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, to your knowledge, who, if anybody, set the village of Kravica on fire as you were evacuating?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: The Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see any of the other surrounding Bosnian Serb hamlets as you were escaping towards Opravdici?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which hamlets could you see?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Donji Mratinci, Siljkovici, Magasici, and then you couldn't see Mandici further along, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Eric, did you ever after January 7th, 1993, go back to your village of Kravica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes. When we were attacking our village, when we were taking it back. I think this was on the 15th of March. I took part in the liberation of my village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that recapture of the village by Bosnian Serbs, did the fighting to recapture the village take place in the centre of the village or did it take place on the surrounding mountainsides?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: On the surrounding mountainsides, and there wasn't really any particular fighting. The Muslims were not really dug in. They were just really holding some approaches to the village and some elevations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You returned to your village of Kravica on the 15th of March, 1993. What did the houses and the buildings look like?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: We came back. They were all burned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you give an estimate, if permitted by Defence counsel, of what percentage of houses in the village of Kravica were burned or destroyed.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: I didn't really understand the question very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, might I just repeat it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to know out of the different houses in Kravica, how many, what percentage, what number, an estimate, of these houses were burned or destroyed.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: All of it, everything that could be burned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have a chance to go back to your house in Kravica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: When we entered the village, my house is in the middle of the village, in the centre of the village. I spent the night in my house. I lit a fire in the middle of the room and I warmed myself by the fire because it was cold.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had your house also been burned?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Down to the ground. As much as it could burn; everything was burned that could burn.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, in your opinion was the burning of the houses in Kravica a result of the January 7th, 1993 attack or was it caused by the March 15th, 1993 recapture of Kravica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: All the houses in the village of Kravica were burned on the 7th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, after you spent the night in your house, did you continue on with the Serb forces to Bratunac and then return to Kravica a few days later?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did a Dr. Stankovic come to Kravica during the time period when you went back to Kravica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, Dr. Stankovic. He was a major then. He was in Kravica. The families of the victims were collecting the bodies of those who died, and in one yard in the centre of the village he looked at all the bodies and photographed them. I was searching for my grandmother and my grandfather because they were killed on the 7th of January.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask now if the usher would hand Mr. Eric a Prosecution Exhibit previously marked 365. These are again a series of photos, but I would state that I believe, Your Honours, we haven't looked at these photos before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Incidentally the map 397 which -- the coloured map which you have been using with this witness, we did not receive a copy of it. We have 396 but we don't have 397.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, you would like the copy with the different markings on it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think that would be useful.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I agree. I think we will have to photocopy that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think we need all the map. If you could photocopy the part where the witness has put his markings.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then we could restrict that to -- okay. I understand that the registrar can do that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: May I, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead. Don't forget that we have lost about 10 minutes because of the technical hitch we had, so try to compensate as much as you can.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Very well, okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, would you look at the photograph being placed on the ELMO now. It will be ERN number -- I'm sorry, it's also on Sanction for the benefit of the Court. It's ERN number 01087901.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes. The parish hall in Kravica near the church. This is where I pass by to go to my field. This is where I used to pass by often.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this house destroyed on January 7th, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could I ask the usher now to place picture ERN number ending in 898, that's 01087898.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, do you recognise this building?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is the community building in Kravica. This is where they would purchase the agricultural products from us, the cattle, raspberries, blueberries. It was the co-operative, the local co-operative.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, was this building used in 1992 to supply food to the Bosnian Serb forces in Kravica and the surrounding area to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, was this building destroyed on January 7th, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Might I rephrase the question. Do you know whether this building was burned in the attack that occurred on January 7th, 1993, Mr. Eric?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would now like to ask the usher to place the next paragraph, ERN number 0187907. I'll ask Mr. Eric:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise this house?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is the house of Raso Milosevic. This is where I evacuated the last wounded. We passed by this house and we were going in the direction of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the name of the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were going in the direction of which what village, Mr. Eric?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Opravdici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move to the next one 7908.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise this house, Mr. Eric, and if so tell us where it is and --

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: This is the house of -- this is near the school, near my family house. It's the house of a man; he's in Djermani. I don't know his name. His father's name is Slavko, but I don't know the name of the person. He's an engineer. He lives in Djermani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this house destroyed in the attack on January 7th, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: It was burned, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next picture. It's 911. 01087911. Mr. Eric, do you recognise this building?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which one, Ms. Sellers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: This is 01 -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no. Which building, because I see three buildings there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, would you point out the different buildings in this photograph you might recognise?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: This is the old schoolhouse, one, two, three. Right. This is the old schoolhouse. This is a house next door and this is a neighbour's house. I know. They burned down completely in the attack of the 7th. They were torched.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, is this the schoolhouse where there were meetings between yourself, Jovan Nikolic, or yourself and Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Up to here is the new schoolhouse; that's where we held the meetings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So were meetings held in the other schoolhouse?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the other schoolhouse was not used for any form of military purposes, Mr. Eric?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Might I move to the next picture, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, do you recognise this building, and if so tell us what it is.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: This is Erto [phoen] Nikolic's house and this is the local shop. It was also torched.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these buildings both torched in the attack of January 7th, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you described the building to the right as the local shop.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this a shop that was used to supply food or supplies to the Bosnian Serb army during 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Might I move to the next picture, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, do you recognise this house?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's Nedjo Nikolic's house in the centre of the village. It was torched and burned down on the 7th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that 1993, in January?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Might I move to the next picture, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the gym of that school, next door another house, and the schoolhouse also burned down on the 7th. Here is the fountain in the middle of the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's ERN number 01087912 for the record. Mr. Eric, I would ask you: Is that the schoolhouse that was used to have meetings sometime between yourself and Jovan Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Might we move to the next picture, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is my uncle's house, Cvijetin Eric torched on the 7th of January, 1993. You can see the roof being put up again.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Might we move to the next picture again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, do you recognise this house?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is the house of my grandfather, Golub Eric, burned down on the 7th of January, 1993. An old house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are these houses you just mentioned now and the house of your uncle, are they located in the village of Kravica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Might we move to the next picture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, would you please tell us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Here is the infirmary, the infirmary where I used to work or the clinic. I worked there throughout the war. You see this building that was torched, that's here, that's it. This used to be the post office and this is the cultural hall where balls and dances were held. There was a cafeteria inside. Here is the street in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, might I ask you whether the cultural hall or the post office were used for military purposes during the summer or fall of 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Might we go to the last and final picture, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, would you -- do you recognise the house in this picture?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this how your house looked when you returned to Kravica on the 15th of March, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was this house destroyed in the attack in Kravica on the 7th of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this the house where your grandparents you said died, were found?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes. My grandmother burned in this room up here. And downstairs I spent the night of the 15th of March. That's the room where I lit a fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Eric.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: If the usher might remove the photos at this point. Your Honour, I would like to tender those photos into evidence for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That will be marked P400. Will that be P400? Do you want to mark them P400/1, 2 in sequence or what? Because I noticed that the ERN numbers are not in sequence --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: No, they're not because we will have witnesses in the same other area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll keep it P400.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, I just have one final question for you. When you returned to Kravica and you saw the property destruction, to your knowledge did the Bosnian Muslim -- pardon me, did you hear me before?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would suggest you repeat the question, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, when you returned to Kravica on March 15th, 1993 and saw the property destruction, to your knowledge did the Bosnian Muslim forces during the attack of January 7th, 1993 distinguish between military targets in Kravica and private homes, businesses, community or public buildings?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No way, no way. No distinction was made. It was all the same to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that they destroyed the buildings and houses in Kravica without distinction to military targets -- military objectives, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perhaps before Madam Vidovic starts. Were there any military targets in the village of Kravica on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, apart from us and those houses there was nothing special. There was no barracks, nothing I can think of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So now you are going to be cross-examined by Madam Vidovic. May I remind you of what I told you before. Your responsibility, duty, obligation, is to answer her questions as fully and truthfully as possible. Madam Vidovic. Cross-examined by Ms. Vidovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Eric. I would only like to ask you to give me brief answers to my questions and whenever possible please answer with a yes or no or I don't know to save time.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, you have been questioned here today as to whether you had been a member of the Crisis Staff. You were indeed a member of the Crisis Staff that had been organised by the SDS in mid-April 1992, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: In terms of establishment, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may ask the usher to put an excerpt from the book "The Bloody Christmas of Kravica Village," pages 42 and 43 on the ELMO. This book was written by Boro Miljanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, I will read two small excerpts from the quoted pages of this book and in this connection I will ask you a couple of questions. So please look at these pages. I will quote now. "In mid-April a Crisis Staff was established and the following persons were elected on to it, Nedjo Nikolic, president; Krsto Cvjetinovic; Radomir Raso Milosevic; Bogoljub Golub Eric; Jovan Nikolic; Mile Milanovic; Dragan Ilic; Luka Bogdanovic; Slavisa Eric, and Nedeljko T. Nikolic. For security reasons, the Crisis Staff cancelled regular tuition, whereas the schoolhouse was turned into a barracks. Territorial units were established. The staff established defence lines in all populated areas from Banjevici, Donje and Gornje Brana, Bacici, Jezero, Mratinjaci, Gornje and Dornje Dolovi, Brezanci, Jasikovaca, Ravni Buljim, Jezestica, (Jaglic, Djermani, Vresinje), Magasici (Mjenice, Radukici, Bozici, Deronjici) through Avdagina Njiva and Mandici up to Bandijera." "There results of the work of the Crisis Staff were visible already with its first activities. People originating from Kravica were willing and ready to help their village including the sending of volunteers from defence. They confirmed this and it was also confirmed by the newly arrived fighters, volunteers, who left their jobs in Belgrade and other places in order to take up arms to defend Kravica. Thus among the first to come from Belgrade was Gordan Nikolic. Then came Milan Milosevic, nicknamed Minja, who immediately took up the organisation of the village defence on the line Banjevici, Ocenovici and Begici. He brought from Belgrade with him about 20 young men from Ocenovici and Banjevici. Weapons and equipment from the storehouses of the Territorial Defence were, to begin with, sufficient. Some of it was gathered and procured from various sides. The black market was in full swing. A great role in those days --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would counsel please slow down. We haven't finished with the excerpt.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A great role in the days of defence was played by Major Ljubomir Tesanovic as well as senior staff sergeant Miroslav Dadic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I ask you, witness, did you -- can you confirm: The Crisis Staff established defence lines on the entire territory of Kravica. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The school building in Kravica was turned into a barracks by the Crisis Staff. Is that correct? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't say so. But it's where the meetings were held in the school house, not in the barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please answer with a yes or no.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Is it true that the cultural hall in Kravica was turned into an arms depot?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did the farmers' co-op serve for in the period between mid-April 1992 and the attack on Kravica on the 7th of January?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. Since it was a farmers' facility fenced in, there were a couple of cows that the villagers were selling that were in that building, indoors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are a medical staff worker?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know what the infirmary and the pharmacy were used for?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Of course I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they used for military purposes?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: When the war broke out, yes, they were used for military purposes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Golub Eric is your grandfather?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How old was he in 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: I don't know. He was born in 1913 or 1914.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a fighting man?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, he died as a fighting man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this part of the book we see a description saying that the Crisis Staff had organised the arming of the people of Kravica from the arms depot of the Territorial Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Just a minute, lady.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please answer my question. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. I don't want you to interrupt each other to start with. That's number one. And secondly, after -- allow, please, an interval of time between question and answer. Because whatever you're saying in the Serbian/Croat language is being translated to us in English, and the interpreters have a very difficult job here, perhaps the most difficult job after ours. They have to catch up with what you are saying all the time and translate, some of them into French and some into English. And if you run the way you are running, they won't make it. Your question again, Madam Vidovic, please. And then allow an interval and then you answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the staff organise the arming of the Kravica population of Serb ethnicity from the depots of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. It was not up to me to deal with that and to think about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, the officers of the former JNA in April and May 1992 arrived in the territory of Kravica to join in the fighting against the Muslims. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Some did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that the staff coordinated the arrival of volunteers from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No. They came on their own.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a minute. Before I ask my next question I would kindly ask that this excerpt from the book "Bloody Christmas in Kravica Village" be given a number.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: May I just say a word now?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will continue to ask you questions about the volunteers.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: But can I just say something in the meantime if that is allowed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are supposed to answer questions. If you think you have not answered a question sufficiently, then you can ask me, tell me what you want to say, and I will consult with the two Judges, and I will decide whether to let you say. But strictly speaking you are to answer questions here, not to make statements.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what I wanted to -- I just wanted to ask one thing, to say something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What do you want to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, this book, "Bloody Christmas in Kravica village," without purporting to diminish the work of this author, Boro Milanovic, a man I don't know at all, the man did a lot of work to write this book, suffered, but how relevant is this book for me to discuss it at all? Because, Mrs. Vidovic, this is not the only book in existence. There are two or three more --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I am asking questions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Eric, when I say "stop," it means stop.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And don't provoke another incident like this because I will treat you differently. You're not here to argue with the lawyers; you're here to answer the questions that they put to you. If you agree with what is suggested to you, you say: I agree. If you don't agree, you say you don't agree and you give the reasons but not beyond that. You're not here to make speeches. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. If I may kindly ask the usher to put 01336196 on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In the meantime, we still haven't given this excerpt from the book a number. This will be exhibit -- Defence Exhibit D?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 35, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 35, D35. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So 01336196. It is instructions to the treasury dated 1st July, 1992 issued by the War Staff, and it originates from the seized documentation of the Bratunac Brigade. It was seized by the OTP. Will you please look at this document.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says here: "Pay out at the expense of the account of the War Staff of Kravica an amount to compensate travel expenses for volunteers Jarovic, Mirko [phoen], under number one, under number two, Zivkovic [phoen], Dragan." Does this mean, Mr. Eric, that the Crisis Staff of Kravica actually paid volunteers?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, might I point out one thing. I would just like to put on the record that learned counsel has shown the document, has referred to the document. The witness has not in any way recognised the document, adhered to the contents of the document at all. So it is going in, we believe, without necessarily having related to the evidence that she is elicited from the witness. We understand very much Your Honour's policy in terms of acceptance or the admission of evidence, but we just wanted to make that clear one time on the record. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Ms. Sellers. May I interrupt you for a minute, Madam Vidovic, and ask the witness a question related to this document. Are you aware that the Kravica Crisis Staff had an account, a bank account, of its own?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no way. No, it didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you have money at your disposal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you show this document again to the witness and ask him whether he recognises the signature at the bottom right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You don't know who that person is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And do you know the two persons mention Mirko Jarovic and Dragan Zivkovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This will be Defence exhibit number D36 for the record.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, the Crisis Staff organised training for the Serb population in advance of the war, much before the war started. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it true that the old schoolhouse in Kravica that you identified a moment ago in the photograph was a training centre?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it true that Ljubo Sobot led the training in 1992 and 1991 in Kravica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No. This is the first time I'm hearing the name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. If I may now ask the usher to show the witness exhibit -- Defence Exhibit D7. It is titled: "List of Staff Members and Logistics of the TO of Kravica." 01320325. Did you see it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, your name features here under number 8. There is also Mr. Nikolic, Jovan Nikolic; Nedjo; and others?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please leaf through this list, turn the next page for instance. On the following page numbered 01320326, 24 members of the artillery are named. Look at those names. Do you know any of these men?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: I do, some of them, but what does it have to do with this case?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will now ask you the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Eric. Mr. Eric, again you have no right to ask Ms. Vidovic what her question has to do with this case. That's up to us, not up to you to decide. You answer her question, otherwise I will have to censure you again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's precisely what I wanted to ask you, Mr. Eric. You are medical staff, you toured the terrain, you gathered the wounded. Let me ask you, where were artillery pieces deployed, the artillery pieces manned by these men?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: I didn't tour the terrain or gather the wounded. I don't know who told you that I did that. I took care of the wounded at the infirmary. The entire time of the war, I worked at the infirmary where the wounded were brought in from all sides. So I'm not familiar of the operational side of either artillery services or any other services. Was I clear enough? Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Didn't you, Mr. Eric, tell us the story not long ago how you were wounded out in the field in the process of gathering the wounded?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: That happened once because there was only one person wounded. If there had been more, I wouldn't have gone out to collect him. They would have been brought to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me go on then with my questioning. Mr. Eric, isn't it true that the entire zone of Kravica was militarised as early as the beginning of the war?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: I don't understand what you mean. What do you mean by "militarised"? What exactly do you imply?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll clarify.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, do clarify.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it the case that the entire territory of Kravica had established lines of defence, units, logistics, artillery pieces deployed, and everything that is implied by logistics and logistical support for armed combat?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: In which period, 1992? Tell me which period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, I was very clear indeed. Will you please follow my questions and answer them briefly. From the beginning of the war until the attack.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I will ask you something else, Mr. Eric. You, which is obvious from your statement today, passed through the area besides Glogova, Suha, Borkovac, Podcaus, Burmjiste [phoen], the outlying settlements of Bratunac; is that true?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No, that's not true. I didn't have any need to go there. I was in Kravica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You explained a little bit earlier that you went between -- you were going back and forth from Bratunac to Glogova?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes. But that's not where that is, Podcaus, that's not the same place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you pass by Glogova, Suha, Borkovac and the outlying areas of Bratunac which is there?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did, those ones that are there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware in that case that there were expulsions and killings of hundreds of Muslim civilians from these villages?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No, not the killing of hundreds, but I am aware that these people were expelled from these villages. But I'm not aware that hundreds of Muslims were killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that at least 100 people were killed in the Vuk Karadzic school in Bratunac at the time?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No, no, I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that the fighters of the Kravica detachment took the lead in the killings of these Muslims from the surrounding villages?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps ever hear of the name of Bato Zivanovic, called Kocanj. He's a person from Kravica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. He's a neighbour of mine. He lived close by. We grew up together. Yes, I did hear about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps hear that he took part in the execution of a large number of people in the village of Borkovac?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Slow down. Once more you are going too fast for the interpreters to catch up. I can see the effort that they are making to catch up with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I apologise. I will repeat my question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is Bato Zivanovic, called Kocanj, from Kravica the one who led the executions in the local Muslim villages, including Borkovac?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it correct, Mr. Eric, that people from Glogova tried to reach their property -- Glogova is their village, a Muslim village, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And stay in their homes in Glogova?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes. But what can I say? Yes, yes, Glogova is their village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it true, Mr. Eric, that they were practically attacked on a daily basis from Kravica and the surrounding villages?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, you also participated in these activities, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to ask the usher to place a document by the Serbian municipality of Bratunac on the ELMO, document by the Crisis Staff number 01/6/92 dated the 13th of April, 1992, which is an order on the forming of staffs, commands, and units of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could the witness please look at the document, especially item 3. If you could look at that, please, I am quoting: "The Crisis Staff shall take all the decisions relating to the use of the Territorial Defence in accordance with the proposals of the commander of the Serbian TO." You were a member of that Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean no, Mr. Eric? Isn't it true that you were a member of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, in Kravica but not in Bratunac. This is an order -- yes, yes, I was a member. Yes, I was a member. I didn't see that this is an order from the Bratunac staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, an order referring to Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was a member. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it true then that the Crisis Staff of Kravica reached decisions on the combat use of their units?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document please be tendered into evidence as a Defence exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's being admitted into evidence as Defence Exhibit D37.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you briefly about a certain part of your testimony today.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that you heard somehow that Mr. Oric commanded --

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know who ordered the attack on Jezestica. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know anything about the structure of the Bosnian army at that time?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Very little.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not have any reliable information, a document or anything like that, based on which you could claim anything in this regard?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is true. I did not have any documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the opinion you voiced here today is not based on any kind of valid data?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I am now going to ask you about the wound you sustained and which you talked about earlier today. At the time you were with your driver Marko Tomic, isn't that so? You were in a yellow van. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was not a medical vehicle?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Well, we didn't have a medical vehicle, madam. This was a vehicle that was marked; it wasn't very visible but it was marked. The vehicle was being used as a medical vehicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it wasn't visibly marked?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Not very visibly marked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Very well. Isn't -- is it correct that at the time there were two volunteers from Serbia with you in that vehicle?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is true. I don't know their names though. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were they going, Mr. Eric?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: They were not going anywhere; they were there on the line. They were not going anywhere. They were in the trenches. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it true, Mr. Eric, that Serbian forces were attacking the Muslim population the whole time, the Muslim population of Glogova, and that you as a medical worker constantly treated the wounded in Glogova from the beginning of the war until the end of 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Please, on the 28th of July there were no Muslim forces in Glogova, no. They were not in Glogova. Could you please check your information. They were in Glogova on the 24th of December, but not before then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you a little earlier whether the Muslim population of Glogova tried to survive, to stay in their homes in Glogova?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No. No, they were not trying to survive there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who were you fighting with in Glogova then?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: We were not fighting with anybody in Glogova; we didn't have anyone in Glogova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will put my question differently.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it true, Mr. Eric, that in those fights around Glogova in this period I am talking about between the beginning of the war and the attack on the 7th of January you had 30 killed and 64 wounded fighters, the majority of them from Kravica, Jezestica, and the surrounding villages. Isn't this true or not?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No, this is not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like the usher to show Mr. Eric our exhibit, Defence Exhibit D22 called: "The List of Wounded in Glogova."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First I would like you to place page 02075887 on the ELMO and then could the witness please look at this page and the page after that.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it true that this is a list of wounded in Glogova. The list ends with number 64?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes. But look --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I -- you said yes. I will now put the question to you and I would like you to respond.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Beside the names of these people from Jezestica and Kravica, I would like to ask you: What did the person on number 1 of the list Andric, Aleksandar, from Nevesinje doing, number 2, Radan Andjic, from Bijeljina. What were they doing? What were these people doing here from Bogojno, from Pernjavor?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: I don't understand. What's in dispute here, Nevesinje, Bijeljina, this is in the former Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I am satisfied with this answer.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: May I --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've said you know who Jovan Nikolic was?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that so. Okay. Now I would like the technical booth to play a video excerpt and before they do that I would just like to be sure that the transcript of this footage has been given to Your Honours, to the Prosecution, and then I would like to ask the technical booth to play a very short videoclip. This is footage which was disclosed to us by the Prosecution, and it's number V003937. And it was confiscated by the Prosecution in the archives of the Bratunac Brigade. It films the formation of the Bratunac Brigade on the 14th of November, 1992 and the assault brigade which is being placed under the command of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, you are giving evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, yes. All right. Very well. Thank you. I am just trying to present this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the technical booth now play this clip, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Have you been commanding so far in this brigade? Is the same thing going to be the same thing? Well, we are from Kravica bound by tradition, and I think this is going to be the same in the future. Kravica has so far given over 30 dead fighters, the same number of civilians, 55 wounded. The territory we hold is 64 [as interpreted] square kilometres, and we have not ceded one inch of this territory. We shall continue to keep that territory. There is no dilemma there. As far as the Bircanska Brigade is concerned, I would like to say that it is the tradition of the 6th East Bosnian Assault Brigade and because of the circumstances the headquarters of that brigade are in Sekovici. And we have a commander such as Andric. We are lucky to have him come in time here and he is our savior. The people from Kravica, we call him Zekic, he is one of the commanders, but Andric stayed. Everybody loves him and appreciates him, and he's become a legend here. Therefore I am glad that everything is finished here. Besides him we also have Colonel Zivanovic here. We were lucky to have him in Rogac on the 6th of September to talk with him. And I think that what is happening with here with our cadres, that is the perspective of the Serbian army in Bosnia. Specifically we have already done a lot Colonel Zivanovic, Lieutenant Colonels Andric and Tesic, who also introduced Captain Vaso. These are people who are going to be our saviors. We should trust them and Serbian people have accepted them as our own. And I am sure with them we can win this battle. Does that mean that the Bratunac Brigade is going to go on from where the Bircanska Brigade left off? Absolutely. And we have Kravica have the intention of going to the assault brigade being led my Andric so that we can retake that territory. So far we were holding the lines, maintaining the lines, that was our task, to keep these villages. But things are changing now the brigade has been formed. A real army. We, people from Kravica, would like to go ahead with the assault battalion led by Andric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, have you seen this footage?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, is it true that the Kravica detachment was completely incorporated into the military structure of the Army of Republika Srpska and that it was a part of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we're not talking about the village guards here but a part of the army?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes. This was later. It turned itself into the army. Yes. It became part of the true army. You are right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that the Bratunac Brigade was established on the 14th of November, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: I don't know. That's something that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree that the person whom you saw in this footage, Jovan Nikolic, was the commander of the Kravica detachment?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Jovan Nikolic was there, but whether he was a commander or not, if you say so, then yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He mentioned General Milenko Zivanovic. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that General Milenko Zivanovic at the time was the commander of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I wasn't really interested in that. It's possible that he was, but I wasn't following that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, you were a member of the Crisis Staff; that's a political function. This presupposes that you had certain information of a military nature at your disposal. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No. I told you that I was a member of the staff by establishment, so there's a difference there. I think this is important to be a member of the staff, Crisis Staff, and to be a member of the staff by establishment. But you can take it as you like, however you feel fit, is necessary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Eric. I'm now going to ask you something else. Is it true in this period --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment before you proceed with the next question. The videoclip that we saw, is that being tendered by the Defence as an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So that will be D38.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, it will be D38 and the transcript would be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The translation --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: There's a B/C/S transcript to be D38.1, and the translation with the English version of D38.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, is it true that in that period the Drina Corps, including the units of the Kravica detachment, held under siege small enclaves including Konjevic Polje which you showed in response to a Prosecutor's question today and certain villages such as Cerska and others. Is it true that 80.000 Muslims from that area were under siege in November 1992, under siege by the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: They were under siege, but the figure of 80.000 seems too high to be believable. The whole area didn't have that population. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. But they were under siege?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Under siege or not, we were defending ourselves, fending off their attacks. If they suddenly found themselves under siege, too bad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Eric, is it true that after the establishment of the Bratunac Brigade an order was issued to all Serb units in the area of Podrinje, the Drina Valley, including the Kravica units, to expel or destroy the remaining Muslim population that had been trying to survive there?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Perhaps, but I hadn't seen or heard such an order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that on the 24th December, 1992 fierce fighting took place around Kravica and the neighbouring Glogova and it lasted all the way up to the 7th of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: On the 24th, Glogova was taken and the fighting ceased. Apart from sporadic shooting, there was no more fighting except from the direction of Bratunac when their units tried to lift the blockade unsuccessfully. I don't believe there was shooting from our side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, please. When you say Glogova was taken, Glogova is a Muslim village?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who do you think it was taken by?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: The Muslims, again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that Muslims were trying to go back to their homes, their property, their food?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes. But there was no property or food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You, Mr. Eric, were aware that continuous fighting lasted up to the 7th of January. Isn't it true that you were admitting wounded on the 5th and the 6th of January?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Maybe one or two at a time. I can't remember exactly. I can't tell you the names of these people.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may ask the usher now to put on the ELMO a document of the command of the Bratunac Brigade number 01320545, which is a list of the fighting men of the 4th Battalion. So a list of the fighting men of the 4th Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade who on the 24th of December, 1992 lost their lives in the village of Glogova.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, this fighting around Glogova was therefore under way.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: What do you mean was under way? This was the 24th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, it is the 24th. What were the Serb fighters doing in the Muslim village of Glogova on that day?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: They were not in the Muslim village of Glogova; they were at positions near Glogova, from Hranca on one side to Magasici, and Bozici on the other side. They were never in Glogova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps we should take the break now if the Trial Chamber --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, we can have a break now. But how do you know these things? Were you there during the fighting on the 24th? How do you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. know the exact position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The positions of those units?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, the position of these persons who were killed. Because you said -- you were very precise. "They were not in the Muslim village of Glogova; they were at positions near Glogova, from Hranca on one side to Magasici and Bozici on the other side. They were never in Glogova." How -- were you there during the fighting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I was passing through Glogova whenever I had wounded men with me and on other occasions. And since I grew up and worked in Bratunac, I know those villages and the environs like the back of my hand. So I know where the soldiers were. It was a concern for me. I was passing through Glogova and I knew where they were and were they weren't. I knew where approximately they were located.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But I do remind you that one of the very early questions that Madam Vidovic put to you was precisely whether you were going round collecting bodies, collecting the sick, et cetera, and you were very precise there. You said, no, no, no, that you were in your clinic and tending to the sick and the wounded that were taken there and that you were there -- definitely not going round. It seems that you were going round.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. As the fighting became more intensive and as the units which at the outset had been poorly organised and hastily hatched got better, I started touring. And throughout the world you will find it a rule for medical staff to inspect, to tour the lines, not to fortify them of course. But it is the duty of medical staff to be familiar with the positions and even tour the personnel holding those positions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Judge Eser would like to put a question to you before we go on break.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: You mentioned that you knew from which parts or which places the attack was led for, but before you had said you would not know exactly what was going on. Now, when you explained to us that you knew where normally soldiers were posted, does this imply that you also knew the exact place from which the concrete attack on the 24th of December was led from? Is there a difference between knowing where normally soldiers are posted and the exact place, the concrete place, where an attack on a certain day and a certain time was performed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understood your question and I will try to answer specifically. When early in the morning on Christmas Day I received a visit from Miladinovic, Miladin, I knew that he had come from Dolijani, that's where he was wounded because he was a local of the village defending his village. And when Zeljko Radovic came in, I knew of course that he was coming from Siljkovici, because that's where he was deployed. And as people came in, I would know from which defence line they were coming.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will have a short break of 25 minutes. And please try to be as punctual and hopefully we won't have technical problems. Do you think you're still on track, able to finish by quarter to 2.00?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just before we rise, if I may ask for this exhibit to be given a number. The last exhibit dated the 24th of December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This will be D39. Correct? So this will be Defence Exhibit D39. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We left off on the discussion about the fighting around Glogova and the 24th of December. I will now ask you a question, Mr. Eric. This fighting around Glogova, it was not spontaneous, was it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is the case that it was planned and ordered, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No, it wasn't ordered.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may ask the usher to put on the ELMO Defence Exhibit D25.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, Witness, look at this report of the Bratunac Brigade to the command of the Drina Corps dated 4th January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Be so kind as to look at the last sentence of para 1 of the document which says: "We assume that in the area of Glogova there remains about 200 armed Turks." Then para 2 goes: "Our forces are carrying out active operations in the area of villages of Tatar, Maljevo, Vinjesta [phoen], Kravica, and Velika Glogova village. Vladosic [phoen], Petkovici, Brezanci, Sandici, Saonik, and so on. Mr. Eric, isn't it the case that the fighting around Glogova did not stop until the 7th of January?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: If you're talking about from Bratunac, the direction from Bratunac, then the answer is yes. But not from Kravica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was: The fighting in the area of Glogova did not stop until the 7th of January?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you mean to say that people from Kravica were not involved in this fighting?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Were they involved. Assault units did not take part. As for people, it's difficult to say. It's difficult to say whether some individual people were involved. It's possible they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that all the way up to the 7th of January, 1992 [as interpreted] you were admitting wounded men from Glogova, Serb soldiers wounded in Glogova?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may now ask Defence Exhibit D26 to be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have had a look at the document. Doesn't it say here that these men had been wounded in Glogova and were undergoing out-patient treatment?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes. But from the direction of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, my question was: Did you admit wounded men at your infirmary? Were you aware of this fighting and the fact that people were getting wounded there?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: I was aware but these people never came to me. Those people came from Bratunac and returned to Bratunac. Why would they go through Glogova? It's possible that someone was in the meantime wounded but not these people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just said you were aware --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is confusing. You see the transcript is -- says: "I was aware but these people never came to me. Those people came from Bratunac and returned to Bratunac. Why would they go through Glogova? It's possible that someone was in the meantime wounded but not these people." This goes diametrically opposed to what the document itself says. So we need to clarify this. Are you contesting that these persons that -- whose names appear on the document that you have in front of you were indeed or in truth wounded on the 5th of January while they were fighting in Glogova? Are you denying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They did not come to me for medical assistance in Kravica; that's what I'm contesting.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. This answer satisfies my question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, I will now ask you something about the attack itself.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not see the attackers, did you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't see them at any one time.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: I did. Only as we were retreating, from a distance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to identify, to tell whether they were soldiers or civilians? Did you see any civilians among the attackers?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: No, no. I don't know who they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you a different question now. Today in response to another question of mine referring to artillery personnel manning artillery pieces, you said that you did not know where the artillery was positioned. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you still maintain that you were not aware where artillery pieces were deployed?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Prosecutor has referred today to the statement of this witness from 2001 and so have I.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you gave this statement to the Prosecutor in 2001?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Of course I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You signed it then?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were cautioned on that occasion that you are duty-bound to tell the truth?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then on that occasion on page 03062708 of that statement in B/C/S --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please look at this B/C/S version. Page 02062541 of the English version, third paragraph.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said -- please look at it.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: I know it. I know it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "I was aware that on the hill at Siljkovici an artillery piece was deployed." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes. But is one artillery piece tantamount to artillery? If that is the same as artillery, you are free to understand it that way. It's true that there was one artillery weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Today, Mr. Eric, you said that you didn't know where artillery pieces were deployed.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: I wasn't talking about one artillery piece; I was talking about artillery. Do you feel the difference? It's not the same thing, an artillery piece and artillery as such. Will you agree with me? No, you won't. It's up to you. No problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Eric.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are going to end up to trouble if you continue like this. I told you to answer the question and you don't discuss -- argue with the lawyer. Don't give me that because I will have to censure you and I will have to punish you, if you continue like that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I will not continue like that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic is doing her duty here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You promised me in the beginning that you will not discriminate between the Prosecution and the Defence, and I noticed that while you had absolutely no problems in answering the questions coming from the Prosecution and you answered them without any arguments and with a lot of tranquility, you are not behaving the same way with the Defence counsel and you are not reacting the same way in trying to answer the questions that are coming from the Defence. That's what you promised me in the beginning. Let's go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was: Did you know the people who were servicing the artillery weapons?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you responded that you did not?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: This particular artillery weapon, piece.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Mr. Eric, you agree that this artillery piece was located on the Siljkovici hill?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree that this weapon was the first target of the attack on the Siljkovici hill?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Amongst other things, but Siljkovici was a dominant spot and that is why the attack was first carried out against Siljkovici, with the objective of capturing Siljkovici first.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you specifically whether this artillery weapon was the first target of the attack?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Well, no, no. It wasn't. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to draw the witness's attention to the same paragraph of this statement on the same page, of the statement given on 2001. He said the following -- just one second, please. "I knew that there was an artillery gun fixed on the hill in Siljkovici. This was up on the hill, on the top of the hill. I know that this gun was operated by soldiers Pajkan Gavric, Savljevic, and Radovic. I do not know the first names of the last two. These people were killed during the early stage of the attack. This means very early in the morning. When the Muslims attacked that part of the village, one of the first points of the attack was this gun."

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes. One of the points of attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't agree that it was the first point of attack but it was amongst the initial points of attack.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: When you talk of artillery or artillery piece, could you please describe what you mean with the artillery piece. Was it a gun which needed to be carried by various people or was it some sort of a gun which would be carried by one person or so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Several people could carry it or perhaps it could be pulled by a vehicle. It's a 76-millimetre weapon. I'm not very well versed in that. But it's something -- it's a weapon that could be carried by several people.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, the Kravica region actually had vast quantities of weapons at that time. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Well, it had a substantial amount of weapons but not vast amounts of weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it had substantial -- a substantial quantity of weapons?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher place document -- this is a document of the Light Bratunac Brigade of the 9th of October, 1993, and it has the number 00675503. It was seized from the documentation of the Bratunac Brigade by the Prosecutor's Office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, could you please look at this document?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a report of the brigade of the Drina Corps. Could you please look at this document. Isn't it correct that this document gives the quantities of weapons?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
